verses.text: So we are surrounded by a huge crowd of people who have shown their faith. Let us throw off everything that holds us back, and the sin that so easily trips us up. Let us keep running the race God has set before us, and never give up.

Let us keep our eyes on Jesus. Our faith starts with him, and he makes it complete. Because of the joy waiting for him, he suffered on the cross and did not care about its shame. Now he is sitting at the right hand of God's throne.
Think about Jesus, who put up with so much hatred from sinners. Then you will not get tired and give up.
In your fight against sin, you have not yet had to fight to the point of being killed.
Have you forgotten the encouraging words God speaks to you as his children? "My child, do not think little of the Lord's discipline, and do not give up when he corrects you.
The Lord disciplines everyone he loves, and he corrects everyone he accepts as his child."
Put up with hard times as discipline. God is treating you as his children. What child is never disciplined by their father?
Everyone receives discipline. If you are never disciplined, then you are not really God's children at all.
We all had human fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them for it. So we should be even more willing to obey God, the Father of our spirits, and live!
Our fathers disciplined us for a short time, as they thought best. But God disciplines us for our good, so that we can share in his holiness.
No discipline feels nice at the time. It hurts! But later, those who have been trained by it enjoy peace and a life that is right with God.
So lift up your tired hands, and make your weak knees strong.
Make straight paths for your feet, so that weak legs will not be hurt more, but will be healed.
Try your best to live in peace with everyone, and to live a holy life. No one will see the Lord without it.
Be careful that no one misses out on God's kindness. Make sure no bitterness grows up among you like a weed, to cause trouble and spoil many people.
Make sure no one sins sexually or does not care about God, like Esau. He sold his rights as the oldest son for one meal.
You know that later he wanted his father's blessing, but he was turned away. Even though he begged for it with tears, he could not change what had happened.
You have not come to a mountain you can touch, like Mount Sinai, burning with fire, dark and gloomy, with a storm,
and with the sound of a trumpet and a voice speaking. When the people heard that voice, they begged not to hear another word.
They could not stand the command: "If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be killed with stones."
The sight was so terrible that Moses said, "I am shaking with fear."
Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the Jerusalem in heaven. You have come to thousands and thousands of angels, gathered with joy.

You have come to the gathering of God's firstborn children, whose names are written in heaven. You have come to God, the Judge of all people, and to the spirits of good people who have been made perfect.
You have come to Jesus, who brings the new covenant between God and people. And you have come to his sprinkled blood, which speaks of better things than the blood of Abel.

Be careful not to refuse to listen to God, who is speaking. The people of Israel did not escape when they refused to listen to the one who warned them on earth. So we will certainly not escape if we turn away from the one who warns us from heaven!
Back then, his voice shook the earth. But now he has promised, "Once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens."
The words "once more" show that God will take away everything that can be shaken, everything he has made, so that only what cannot be shaken will remain.
We are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken. So let us be thankful, and worship God in a way that pleases him, with respect and wonder,
because our God is like a fire that burns everything up.
